rule: A 60+ map score must describe the settlement or district as a coherent visitor experience. A detached reserve, monument, museum or other attraction remains available under See but cannot by itself make the settlement a rated destination.

results.name: Monymusk
settlementIndependentEvidence: Coherent planned granite village and square
Medieval church and priory story embedded in the village core
Council conservation-area character and short local walks
standaloneAttractionsExcludedFromScore: Private Monymusk House
Private Monymusk Cross
Pitfichie and wider Bennachie experiences
results.rationale: The historic townscape is itself the visit; the score does not depend on the private estate or out-of-boundary countryside attractions.

results.name: Kemnay
settlementIndependentEvidence: Granite-quarry village identity
Place of Origin and Kemnay Steens integrated into the settlement landscape
Exact-town treasure trail and local walking/cycling circuits
standaloneAttractionsExcludedFromScore: Castle Fraser
Bennachie
Other nearby Garioch attractions
results.rationale: Kemnay has a coherent in-town art, granite and walking offer. Nearby Castle Fraser and Bennachie remain context only and do not support the score.

results.name: Kintore
settlementIndependentEvidence: Compact historic royal-burgh core
Town House, parish church and Pictish stone in the settlement
Official Kintore walking routes
standaloneAttractionsExcludedFromScore: Hallforest Castle
Broomend of Crichie
Wider A96 archaeological landscape outside the visitor boundary
results.rationale: The burgh core, Pictish stone and town routes form a genuine short stop without borrowing the surrounding archaeological sites.

results.name: Bridge of Don
settlementIndependentEvidence: Aberdeen City Council's map-led Bridge of Don community heritage trail
A coherent lower-Don route linking both crossings, Balgownie townscape and the river
Several independently useful district walking sections rather than one isolated attraction
standaloneAttractionsExcludedFromScore: Donmouth Local Nature Reserve as a separately scored See place
Scotstown Moor Local Nature Reserve as a separately scored See place
Brig o' Balgownie as a separately scored See place
results.rationale: This is the closest borderline case, but it still qualifies because the official district trail makes the place a coherent half-day river-and-heritage visit. The individual reserves and bridges remain separately visible under See and are not treated as the district itself.

results.name: Old Aberdeen
settlementIndependentEvidence: Exceptionally coherent historic university and cathedral quarter
Dense, walkable historic townscape
Multiple official district heritage trails and public gardens
results.rationale: Old Aberdeen's settlement fabric is itself a major visitor experience; its score is not a proxy for a detached attraction.

results.name: Aberdeen
settlementIndependentEvidence: Destination-scale museums, granite architecture, maritime heritage, parks and culture
A deep official city trail network
Sufficient independent experiences for a multi-day city visit
standaloneAttractionsExcludedFromScore: Old Aberdeen is separately rated
Torry and Greyhope Bay are separately rated
Outlying city nature reserves remain separate See places
results.rationale: Aberdeen comfortably qualifies as a destination city after separating the independently audited Old Aberdeen and Torry guides.

results.name: Torry
settlementIndependentEvidence: Distinct historic fishing and harbour district
Four official Torry-specific churches, coastal, industrial-maritime and urban trails
Walkable district heritage extending beyond the Battery
standaloneAttractionsExcludedFromScore: Torry Battery and Greyhope Bay remain a separately scored See place
Nigg and central Aberdeen attractions are outside the settlement score
results.rationale: The Battery is the strongest See place, but Torry still has enough district-specific townscape and trail depth to qualify without transferring the Battery's score to the settlement.

results.name: Cove Bay
settlementIndependentEvidence: Historic fishing-village core and 1878 harbour
Documented Cove-specific coastal and community circuit
Settlement-linked fishwife and fishing heritage
standaloneAttractionsExcludedFromScore: Torry, Greyhope Bay, Doonies and Nigg Bay
results.rationale: Cove Bay is a modest but genuine historic fishing-settlement stop; its harbour is part of the old village rather than a remote attraction lending it a score.

results.name: Peterculter
settlementIndependentEvidence: Village heritage centre in the historic core
Culter Explorer village heritage walks and mapped local path network
Culter Burn, mill landscape and Deeside Way connection from the settlement
standaloneAttractionsExcludedFromScore: Maryculter attractions south of the Dee
Easter Anguston Farm and other Peterculter-postcode sites outside the boundary
results.rationale: The museum is not the sole support: Peterculter has a coherent in-boundary village, burn and walking offer, while postal-address attractions outside the settlement remain excluded.

comparison: Kincorth remains below 60 because its case depended on the separate Kincorth Hill Local Nature Reserve and did not have a comparable settlement-wide visitor offer.
